description: Investigate and recover from Git history problems with hypothesis-driven, read-only-first methods: find when/where a bug or change was introduced (bisect, pickaxe, line-history blame), recover lost commits, branches, stashes and dropped work (reflog, fsck), and reason about what gc and expiry will delete. Use when someone asks "who/when/why did this change", "I lost my commits after reset/rebase/force-push", "find the commit that broke X", "recover a deleted branch or dropped stash", or "did this secret ever enter history". Not for everyday branching or merging (use git-workflow, git-merge-conflicts), and history rewriting or secret purges are out of scope until the user explicitly authorizes them.
